card.essence: The 'weather-cock among remedies' — mild, gentle, tearful disposition with symptoms as changeable as the wind. Pre-eminently a female remedy for plethoric, yielding individuals who crave open air and sympathy yet are chilly and thirstless. Thick, bland, yellowish-green discharges from all mucous membranes. Often indicated after puberty disturbances, suppressed menses, or abuse of iron tonics.

keynotes.text: Mild, gentle, yielding disposition; weeps easily, seeks sympathy
Craves open air; always feels better there, though chilly
Thick, bland, yellowish-green discharges from all mucous membranes
Symptoms ever changing; no two stools alike, no two chills alike
Pains shift rapidly; accompanied by constant chilliness
First serious impairment of health referred to puberty; 'never been well since'

modalities_worse.text: Warm room, warm air, warm applications
Rich, fat food (pork, pastry, cakes, ice-cream)
Rest; beginning motion; lying on left or painless side

modalities_better.text: Cold applications, cold food and drink

mentals: Weeps easily; tearful, timid, irresolute; can hardly give symptoms for weeping
Craves sympathy and consolation; children like fuss and caresses
Easily discouraged; full of anxiety with forebodings
Mild, gentle, yielding — yet peevish, touchy, easily offended
Changeable mood: irritable, then tearful, then mild again
Fears evening, dark, being alone, ghosts; morbid dread of opposite sex
Religious melancholy, fanatical; given to extremes of pleasure and pain
Puerperal or menopausal insanity: sits taciturn, answers only 'yes' or 'no'
physicals: Thick, bland, yellowish-green mucus from eyes, nose, vagina, chest
Menses: too late, scanty, suppressed from wet feet; irregular, intermittent flow
Dysmenorrhoea with intense pain, restlessness, tossing; flows more during day
Threatened abortion: flow ceases then returns with increased force
Gastric disturbances: averse to fat, warm food; thirstless; all-gone sensation
Bad taste in morning; dry mouth without thirst; wants mouth washed frequently
Toothache relieved by cold water in mouth
Diarrhoea: watery, changeable, worse night; after fruit, ice-cream, rich food
Coryza: stoppage in evening or in warm room; loss of smell
Styes, especially upper lid; ophthalmia neonatorum; thick yellow eye discharge
Otorrhoea: thick, bland, offensive; diminished hearing
Cough: dry evening, loose morning; from tickling in epigastrium; must sit up
Air hunger; cannot breathe in warm room; worse lying on left side
Pains: drawing, tearing, erratic; appear suddenly, leave gradually
Veins full, varicose; venous congestion; passive haemorrhages
Lies with hands above head; wants head high; uncomfortable with one pillow
clinical: Chlorosis, anaemia at puberty ('never well since'); delayed first menstruation
Measles: badly managed; otitis, ophthalmia, or bronchitis after suppressed eruption
Mumps with metastasis to mammae or testicles
Gastric derangements from iron tonics, quinine, chamomile, tea-drinking
Subacute conjunctivitis with dyspepsia; gonorrhoeal ophthalmia
Catarrhal otitis; diminished hearing as if ear stuffed
Retained placenta; weak labour pains; after-pains
Rheumatism: pains shift from joint to joint with swelling and redness
Cholera infantum, entero-colitis in hot weather; no two stools alike
Phlegmasia alba dolens; varicose ulcers with hard glistening areolae
Nocturnal enuresis; involuntary micturition with cough or flatus

differentials.note: Nux: irritable, irascible, chilly yet warm room comfortable. Pulsatilla: mild, weepy, warm room intolerable despite chilliness.
Sepia: tearful but with marked irritability, anger, indifference to loved ones. Pulsatilla: mild, seeks consolation.
Nat-m: tearful but consolation aggravates; patient hides grief. Pulsatilla: consolation ameliorates; seeks sympathy.
Cham: violent anger, snappish, spiteful. Pulsatilla: peevish but never irascible; mild temperament.
Ignatia: sad but hides grief from others; contradictory, hysterical. Pulsatilla: seeks sympathy openly; changeableness more somatic.
Silica is the chronic of Pulsatilla in nearly all ailments.
Lyc: weeps when thanked. Pulsatilla: weeps easily, almost impossible to detail ailments without weeping.
Stannum: tearful, discouraged over chest symptoms, fears decline. Pulsatilla: broader tearfulness with gastric/menstrual focus.

cautions: Often abused; do not prescribe on gender or hair colour alone — mental state must match
Antidote to chamomile, iron, quinine, mercury, sulphur (chronic abuse)
Complementary to Kali muriaticum, Lycopodium, Silicea, Sulphuricum acidum
Silicea is the chronic; one of the best remedies to begin treatment of a chronic case
